interactions.summary: Students first define shadow in Platonic terms as a two-dimensional imitation of reality or an instantiated form perceived when light hits matter.

Other students offer moral and optical readings of the shadow as Dante's leftover dirt from hell, an eclipse of light, or simply blocked light, while Jiang keeps pressing them for the metaphor's real target.

Jiang rejects abstract guesses like ego or projection, and a student finally returns to the cave allegory by calling the shadow a kind of illusory knowledge or absence of God, though the answer remains unresolved inside this packet.

speaker_notes.note: The end of the student's answer is noisy and overlaps with Jiang; the stable point is that the student connects cave shadows with illusion and partial knowledge.

claims.claim: Students initially interpret shadow as a reduced imitation of reality: something derivative, two-dimensional, and not the thing itself.
One student moralizes the shadow as residue from Dante's uncleanness in hell, suggesting that the living pilgrim still carries something negative forward into purification.
Another line of student interpretation treats shadow physically as eclipse or light blocked by matter, staying at the level of optics rather than metaphor.

Jiang's repeated pushback shows that none of these answers reaches the metaphor he wants; he is pressing the class past optics and vague abstractions toward a more exact spiritual or psychological reading.
The final student answer in the packet reconnects the image to Plato's cave by calling shadow a projection that offers only illusory knowledge and perhaps marks separation from God.

signature_moments.moment: A student imagines Dante's shadow as the dirty residue he brought with him out of hell.
signature_moments.source_phrase: still like dirty of his shadow
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's most morally charged student attempt to interpret the image before Jiang gives the answer.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang keeps swatting away every abstract answer and demanding the actual metaphor.
signature_moments.source_phrase: shadow is a metaphor for what
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shows his pedagogical style: relentless pressure until the interpretive key is named precisely.

signature_moments.moment: The class circles back to Plato's cave, where shadows become projection and illusion-knowledge rather than reality.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the shadow on the wall is the projection
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It narrows the field of interpretation just before Jiang states the stronger answer in the next packet.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The students' first-pass Platonic definition of a shadow as a flattened likeness rather than reality itself.
A student's attempt to read the shadow morally as residual impurity carried into purification.
A student's phrase for the cave-level knowledge one gets from projections rather than from reality itself.

chronology_notes.note: This packet is a suspended interpretive search: the class tests optical, moral, and Platonic meanings of the shadow, but Jiang has not yet accepted any answer and the decisive reading is deferred to the next packet.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student's appeal to Platonic forms is syntactically rough in the ASR, so the packet preserves only the stable claim that the shadow is understood as a perceptible instantiation rather than ultimate reality.
The end of the final student answer is clipped and overlaps with Jiang, so 'absence of God' and 'fame' are left as tentative fragments rather than settled claims inside this packet.
